Hi Marissa / Rishi,

We are moving toward a final evaluation of Redwood for inference serving. Before we commit, DataCo needs a short mutual action plan that includes a performance benchmarking window and concrete pass/fail criteria (latency, throughput, TTFT, concurrency). We have an internal deadline to finalize vendor selection by Feb 28.

High-level asks:
- A one-page MAP with the benchmarking plan and responsibilities
- Access to a staging/test environment and short-lived test credentials
- A proposed load window (we prefer off-peak nights)
- Definition of TTFT for your platform (how you measure first-token time vs token-generation)

Can you confirm feasibility and a proposed schedule? If we can get the MAP and a staging key this week, we can schedule tests the week of Feb 18.

Thanks,
Emily Santos
Senior SRE, DataCo

Thanks Emily — great to see the timelines. I attached a draft MAP and a lightweight benchmarking plan (MAP-DataCo-PerfPlan-v1.xlsx). Key highlights we propose:

- Metrics: median P50 and P95 token latency, end-to-end TTFT (client request -> first token returned), sustained throughput (requests/sec) at target concurrency, and memory/GPU utilization.
- Concurrency model: scale tests at 1, 5, 25, 100 concurrent sessions; sustained 5-minute steady state at each level, plus 5-minute burst tests at +50% of target RPS.
- Pass criteria: P95 TTFT <= 250ms for small prompts (<=128 tokens), sustained throughput >= target RPS with <=5% error rate. We can tighten these once we see your expected workload.
- Logistics: Redwood will provide a staging endpoint, short-lived API key (scoped), and a reference load script. We ask DataCo to whitelist test window and provide a point-of-contact on your side for scheduling.

Proposed test windows: Feb 18 02:00-06:00 PT or Feb 19 02:00-06:00 PT. Please confirm which works better and estimated target RPS.

Attaching: MAP-DataCo-PerfPlan-v1.xlsx (staging plan + responsibilities).

Next steps:
1) You confirm window + target RPS
2) We provision scoped test credentials and share the load script
3) We run smoke tests, then the full runs and deliver a results report integrated into the MAP

If these dates work, I can lock them and loop in Vivek for the test orchestration.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Emily — looping in technical details so you can validate. Summary of the planned benchmarking harness:

- Environment: isolated staging cluster in us-west-2; identical model binary as hosted catalog (same quantization).
- Endpoints: REST generation endpoint (/v1/generate) + streaming websocket for TTFT checks.
- Test accounts/keys: we will issue a scoped API key (read/write limited to test project) that expires in 7 days. Placeholder: test-credentials-stub.txt.
- Measurement definitions:
  * TTFT: measured at the server as timestamp(request_received) -> timestamp(first_byte_sent) and corroborated client-side for network delta.
  * Latency: token-level latency (server-side), and end-to-end per-request median and P95.
  * Throughput: requests/sec successfully completed without error over 5-minute windows.

- Load profile: recreate your sample traffic pattern if you provide a trace; otherwise:
  * 10k warmup requests at 1 concurrent session
  * step to 100 concurrent sessions, hold 5 minutes each step (1, 5, 25, 100)
  * burst tests: 5x short bursts (30s) targeting +50% RPS above the sustained target

We can support concurrent bursts up to 2,000 RPS for short tests but will need to coordinate with the infra team (and AWS test team) to avoid cross-tenant throttling — please confirm if that peak is required. If you have a synthetic trace generator, share it and we'll adapt the harness.

I will provision the key once we confirm the exact test window and contract for the scoped pilot credit.

— Vivek
Senior Backend Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: test-credentials-stub.txt (API key placeholder — actual credential to be delivered securely)
